subject: Archaeology
title: Monte Albán: City in the Clouds
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Monte Albán: City in the Clouds.

hook.text: The Zapotec people flattened an entire mountaintop in Mexico to build a city above the clouds.

buildup.text: Monte Albán thrived for 1,300 years starting around 500 BCE, housing 25,000 people at its peak.

discovery.text: Alfonso Caso excavated it in 1931 and found Tomb 7 — one of the richest burials ever found in the Americas.

twist.text: The tomb's gold and jade treasures were Mixtec, not Zapotec. A later culture reused the Zapotec burial.

climax.text: The Zapotec had writing, astronomy, and a calendar before the Maya, but history barely remembers them.

punchline.text: They built a city on a mountain and still got overlooked by history.

quiz.question: What surprise did Tomb 7 at Monte Albán reveal?
options: It contained Roman coins proving transatlantic contact
The rich treasures inside were Mixtec, not Zapotec — a later culture reused the burial
The tomb was empty, suggesting it had been robbed in antiquity

details.summary: Monte Albán, built atop a leveled mountaintop in Oaxaca, Mexico, around 500 BCE, was the capital of the Zapotec civilization for over a thousand years. Its monumental plazas, observatory, carved stone monuments, and tombs demonstrate one of Mesoamerica's most enduring and sophisticated cultures.
details.whyItMatters: Monte Albán's mountaintop location required massive landscape engineering, demonstrating the Zapotec civilization's organizational capacity.
takeaways: Built on a flattened mountaintop in Oaxaca, Mexico, around 500 BCE
Capital of the Zapotec civilization for over 1,000 years
Features carved stone monuments called danzantes

faq.question: What are the danzantes of Monte Albán?
faq.answer: Stone slabs carved with contorted human figures, once thought to be dancers. Modern scholars interpret them as depictions of slain or tortured captives — early propaganda displaying conquered enemies. They represent some of the earliest writing in Mesoamerica.

faq.question: Why was Monte Albán built on a mountaintop?
faq.answer: The elevated position provided strategic visibility over the surrounding valleys and a neutral meeting point between three valley communities. The massive effort required to flatten the summit and build on it demonstrated political power and may have had cosmological significance.
